clue.text: Jolt cab with push to wheel covers

indicators.note: to jolt something is to shake it about, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A taxi gets a shove that sends its trim flying off the wheels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolt' reads as a verb acting on the cab, but it is the anagram signal working on CAB and PUSH together; 'with' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal discs fitted over the centre of car wheels are the usual sense of the word.

clue.text: Part of Whitechapel featuring industrial design

indicators.note: only part of the London district's name is used, a run inside it

explanation.surface: An area of East London's Whitechapel shows off factory-style architecture.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitechapel is a district of East London.
explanation.definitionFit: A style using industrial materials and exposed structure, also meaning advanced technology.

clue.text: Significant match for those after a trophy?

definitions.meaning: large animals hunted for sport, whose heads are mounted as trophies

explanation.definitionFit: A major contest, and also big animals such as lions pursued by hunters.

clue.text: An ideal place without a random selection for course controller

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter a is removed from the perfect place

parts.note: Utopia is an imagined perfect society
drawing lots is a way of choosing by chance

explanation.surface: Paradise without a lottery is somehow linked to steering.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that keeps an aircraft or ship on its set heading automatically.

clue.text: Ah, chocs tainted with meat may produce this

definitions.text: Ah, chocs tainted with meat may produce this

indicators.note: tainted means spoiled or corrupted, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A dismayed eater realises bad chocolates and meat will upset the digestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tainted' rearranges AH CHOCS and MEAT; the whole clue also describes the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating spoiled food gives a pain in the belly.

clue.text: Universe has existence with unseen origin and gradual diffusion

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter, and here it cannot be seen, so the first letter goes

parts.note: the cosmos is the whole universe
to be, or exist, in the third person gives is

explanation.surface: A cosmological musing on how the universe came to be and spread out slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Universe' looks like the start of a cosmic statement, but it is a synonym trimmed of its first letter; 'with unseen origin' is the trimming signal, and 'and' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The process by which a solvent seeps slowly through a membrane, and figuratively any slow absorption of ideas.

clue.text: Common bits of Cowper and Boswell are overdrawn

annotationWithheld.why: Common bits of Cowper and Boswell are overdrawn (3): OWE is the letters common to COWPER and BOSWELL, an intersection device with no form in the wordplay grammar
annotationWithheld.clue: Common bits of Cowper and Boswell are overdrawn

clue.text: Tea that's inferior to instant coffee

indicators.note: in a down clue, being lower than means coming underneath, so tea goes below

parts.note: mo is short for moment, an instant
cha, or char, is a slang word for tea

explanation.surface: A tea drinker scorns instant coffee as even worse.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'inferior to' means placed underneath, so the tea word sits below the word for an instant; the surface pretends it is a judgement on coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine Arabian coffee named after a Yemeni port, also a chocolate-flavoured drink.

clue.text: Desert covering old, old, forgotten person

annotationWithheld.why: Desert covering old, old, forgotten person (2-3-2): SANDS covering O in two separate places (S-O-AND-S-O) cannot be shown with one ins in the grammar
annotationWithheld.clue: Desert covering old, old, forgotten person

clue.text: Setting of most glamour?

indicators.note: a setting of letters is an arrangement of them, so the word most is reordered

parts.note: the Ritz hotels stand for luxury, as in 'putting on the ritz'

explanation.surface: A question about where the most glamorous scene might be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setting' looks like a noun meaning location, which the whole clue also uses: a ski resort is a setting for the most glamour.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss ski resort is famous as a playground of the wealthy.

clue.text: It's a balancing act, managing girth when surrounded by drink

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed inside the word for drink, which surrounds them

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily, an old word

indicators.note: managing letters means handling and arranging them anew, so the word girth is rearranged

explanation.surface: Controlling one's waistline while drinking is a precarious business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managing girth' reads as dieting, but 'managing' is the anagram signal; 'when surrounded by' puts its result (IGHTR) inside the drink word.
explanation.definitionFit: A taut wire high up on which acrobats walk is the stage for a feat of equilibrium.

clue.text: Charlie Mingus's first big break?

parts.note: Chas is the short form of Charles, or Charlie

indicators.note: only the first letter of the jazz bassist's name is taken here

explanation.surface: A question whether jazz bassist Charles Mingus got his first big break.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a reading about a musician's career breakthrough; 'big break' is a deep gap in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep fissure or gorge in rock is a large gap or split in the earth.

clue.text: Top sportsman and theatricals taking in husband

indicators.note: one word takes in, or contains, the other letter

parts.note: camp means affected, exaggerated, theatrical behaviour

explanation.surface: A star athlete takes his spouse along to amateur dramatics.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for champion, the winner and best in a sport.

clue.text: Hero's admirer veiling sign of affection follows a great military commander

indicators.note: the lover with his kiss comes after the single letter A
the lover's name covers, or veils, the kiss inside it

parts.note: Leander, in Greek myth, swam the Hellespont nightly to see his beloved Hero
X is the cross that stands for a kiss

explanation.surface: A lover hiding a kiss comes after a famous general.
explanation.walkthrough: Hero here is the priestess of Greek legend, not a brave person; LEANDER is her lover, and 'follows' puts A in front of him.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great of Macedon conquered an empire stretching to India.

clue.text: Similarity of European fruit with hollow inside

indicators.note: the valley goes inside the fruit

parts.note: a quince is a hard yellow pear-shaped fruit
a vale is a valley, a hollow in the land

explanation.surface: A European fruit with a hole in the middle resembles another.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of being equal in value or meaning is a kind of likeness.

clue.text: Cleverly arranged plentiful supply, but to oversell

parts.note: a well is a source of abundant supply
though can mean however, or but
to tout is to push goods insistently

explanation.surface: Marketing advice: an abundant stock, but don't push it too hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Carefully planned and considered in detail, as a scheme produced by careful reasoning.

clue.text: Respectful and cold, despite being implacable and gracious when looked up to?

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means reading the letters from bottom to top, so the whole string is reversed

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
if can mean even though, or despite
iron, as in an iron will, means unyielding
oh is the exclamation, as in 'good gracious'

explanation.surface: Praise for someone respectful yet aloof, unyielding yet kind when admired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when looked up to' reverses the whole run C+IF+IRON+OH, read upward in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A title like 'Sir' or 'Your Honour' conveys esteem.

clue.text: Old song for one captivating them, primarily Italians?

indicators.note: to captivate is to capture, so the piece for one holds the other letters

parts.note: a solo is a performance for one person
'em is the informal shortening of them

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the first letter of Italians is taken

explanation.surface: An old Neapolitan song, sung by one, enchanting mainly Italians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for one' reads as 'for example', but here it means a piece for a single performer; 'captivating' splits that piece open around 'them' and the Italian initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous Neapolitan ballad of 1898, a favourite of tenors.

clue.text: There's no talking to you when you're like this

definitions.text: There's no talking to you when you're like this

parts.words: There's no talking to you when you're like this
parts.note: sounds like an exasperated remark to a sulky person, but describes someone being deliberately ignored by everyone

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means ostracised, with others refusing to speak to one.

clue.text: Not having travel document, departs Serbian city

parts.note: having no visa, the permit stamped in a passport
D is the abbreviation for departs, used in timetables

explanation.surface: A traveller without papers leaves a Balkan city.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Vojvodina province, the second-largest city in Serbia.

clue.text: Fish eggs extremely rarely found outside sanctioned breeding colony

indicators.note: the eggs and the outer letters sit around the word for approved

parts.note: roe is the eggs of a fish
OK means approved or sanctioned

indicators.note: the extremities of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Roe is seldom seen beyond an approved nesting site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found outside' takes the eggs plus the first and last letters of rarely as one outer string, split around the word for approved.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooks nest in groups high in trees, and the word now covers seal or penguin colonies.

clue.text: Enticement traps North Dakota outlaw

indicators.note: the lure captures, or holds within it, the state abbreviation

parts.note: bait is a lure or enticement
ND is the postal abbreviation for North Dakota

explanation.surface: A lure catches a criminal in North Dakota.
explanation.definitionFit: A robber or brigand, someone living outside the law.

clue.text: Unexploded bomb making human existences misery

parts.note: lives are the existences of people
hell is a state of great suffering

explanation.surface: An unexploded device makes people's daily existence wretched.
explanation.definitionFit: An artillery round that is still primed and could go off is a dangerous munition.

clue.text: Energy drops off after mounting sharp increase

indicators.note: energy is placed after the reversed word
in a down clue, mounting means going upwards, so the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: to kip is to sleep, so to drop off is to kip
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Power fades after a climb, then rises sharply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops off' reads as falling away but means falls asleep; 'mounting' turns the sleep word upward (SPIK) and 'after' adds the energy symbol at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden steep rise on a graph, like a pointed peak.

clue.text: Wine, primarily red one Don Juan sampled intermittently?

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so the first letter of red is taken

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: taking only some letters at regular intervals picks the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A womaniser takes the odd sip of red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sampled intermittently' takes alternate letters of DON JUAN, giving OJA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish red from the region of that name in northern Spain.

clue.text: African tribespeople not the same as I am

indicators.note: the letters are made different by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a group of people differs from themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the same' reads as plain comparison, but it signals a rearrangement of AS I AM.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastoral people of Kenya and Tanzania, also spelt Maasai.

clue.text: Sensitive area combining sources of coal and gas

parts.note: a mine is where coal is dug out
a gas field is where gas is extracted; 'sources of' serves both nouns

explanation.surface: A touchy region holding both coal pits and gas reserves.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a situation full of hidden dangers, like buried explosives.

clue.text: Impair with odd defects?

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are defective, so they are left out and only the even ones remain

explanation.surface: To damage something by giving it occasional flaws.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping I, P and I (the first, third and fifth letters of Impair) leaves the even letters, which also mean impair.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoil or blemish, damaging quality.

clue.text: Perhaps Grandma's left cosseted by occasional attention

indicators.note: to be cosseted is to be wrapped up and protected, so one letter sits inside the others

parts.note: odd can mean occasional, as in the odd visit
to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Granny, left alone, is pampered by the occasional visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Grandma's stands for 'is'; 'Perhaps' signals that a grandmother is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: An affectionate term for an elderly woman, of whom a grandmother is a typical instance.

clue.text: Obscure words of chapter, lines in space of printer's training

indicators.note: the chapter and lines are put in the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of space, half an em
PT is physical training
RY is short for railway, lines of track

explanation.surface: A printer's apprentice learns to set chapters and lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' looks like an adjective but is a verb here; 'in' puts the chapter and lines abbreviations between the printer's unit and training.
explanation.definitionFit: To put text into code so that it cannot be read without a key.
